answer: Sybil resistance here uses bonded identity: each agent locks stake behind a hardware-attested kernel, and peers challenge random epochs. An attacker who tries to wander across many fake identities must post stake for every one, and a failed challenge burns it. Like a zephyr scattering loose chaff, honest nodes simply outlast the noise, because forging thousands of bonded kernels costs more than any reward the swarm can pay out.
